text:
sara_finance: Heads up — this morning's nightly billing-report job created ~200 negative stub credits in NetSuite after the pricing experiment rollout. Appears the reconciler dropped the usage_tag field when building the NetSuite invoice payload.


david_recon: ugh. Any sample payload or error?


elaine_ops: found a few 422s from NetSuite in the webhook logs. sample request body (sanitized):

```json
{
  \"customer_id\": \"cus_ABC123\",
  \"lines\": [ { \"amount\": 1234, \"desc\": \"Usage - compute\" } ],
  \"metadata\": { \"experiment\": \"pricing_v2\" }
}
```

Notice there is no usage_tag/plan_tag in the lines anymore — the reconcile step expects that to map revenue accounts and proration. NetSuite returned 422 -> created reversal credits on downstream job.


sara_finance: how did the tag disappear? experiment changed invoice metadata only, not line items right?


elaine_ops: looks like the billing-reconciler normalizes incoming Stripe invoice.webhook payloads by copying invoice.lines[].metadata -> line.tags, but the new experiment added nested metadata at invoice.metadata.experiment_context which overwrote the previous code path. Simple parsing bug.


david_recon: got it. So reconciler saw a mismatch and kicked a corrective credit. Are the affected customers on the same plan? any high-risk accounts?


jenna_pm: ~200 customers, mix of net-new and existing. 12 enterprise customers flagged; finance wants a review before any automated backfill.


matt_support: Can we rollback the experiment toggle? If we flip it off, will nightly stops creating more bad posts?


elaine_ops: Yes — disabling the experiment prevents further malformed payloads. I've paused the nightly billing-report for now and put the reconciler backport onto a hotfix branch.


release-bot: deploy started: billing-reconciler hotfix -> prod (rollout: canary 10%).


david_recon: For remediation I propose: 1) stop nightly job (done), 2) run a targeted backfill that reparses raw Stripe payloads and re-posts corrected NetSuite invoices using original external_id to avoid duplicates, 3) hold journals for 12 enterprise customers for manual review.


sara_finance: +1 to that plan. Finance sign-off required for running the backfill that will touch ledger entries. Jenna can you confirm sign-off window?


jenna_pm: I approve a backfill this weekend (Sat 02:00-06:00 UTC). We want a dry-run report first (list of affected invoice ids + proposed net impact).


elaine_ops: I'll produce a dry-run CSV by EOD with columns: stripe_invoice_id, ns_external_id, old_post_status, corrected_lines, delta_amount. Also will include a small script we run under dry-run flag that doesn't POST but simulates the NS payload.


david_recon: Also adding reconciliation guard: if net impact > $5k for a customer, flag for manual approval. That will prevent big surprises.


sara_finance: Good. After backfill, we need a one-off GL reconciliation run and to notify accounting channel.


matt_support: FYI, alerting updated: any future NetSuite 4xx on invoice post will open a ticket and tag #finance-auto for faster visibility.


elaine_ops: Root cause summary I'll add to the incident doc: parsing priority change from invoice.lines[].metadata -> invoice.metadata.experiment_context caused usage_tag loss. Patch: reconciler now merges both paths and normalizes tags to line.tags; added unit tests + regression eval.


sara_finance: Thanks. Keep me posted on dry-run CSV and canary results.


release-bot: deploy success: billing-reconciler hotfix -> prod canary 10% OK.


elaine_ops: Canary looks clean for 15 minutes. Scheduling the backfill dry-run now.


david_recon: once dry run CSV is in S3 ping here and I'll run the impact calc.


jenna_pm: CSV received. Looks like 197 invoices, gross delta -$14,320 (credits). We'll review enterprise rows tomorrow morning.


sara_finance: Approved to proceed with backfill during the approved window. Please include audit trail for every NS POST.


elaine_ops: will do. Thanks all.


matt_support: tagging this for postmortem and billing runbook update. :white_check_mark:
